chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Aba al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام about a man who prayed on a cloudy day facing other than the qiblah, then the sun rose while he was still within the time. Should he repeat the salat (prayer) if he had prayed facing other than the qiblah? And if he had sought the qiblah to the best of his effort, would his salat (prayer) suffice him? He said: He repeats whatever is still within its time; but when the time has passed, then there is no repetition upon him.

key_terms.الْوَقْتُ: the prescribed time of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَحَرَّى: strove to determine correctly through personal effort
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he repeats the act of worship

ai.seo_question: If someone prayed in the wrong direction of the qiblah and then found out before the time ended, must he repeat the salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who discovers during the prayer time that he had prayed in the wrong direction of the qiblah. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the salat (prayer) must be repeated if its time remains, but once the time has passed, no repetition is required.
